newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge to 3rd straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge to 3rd straight record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended above the 5,200-point mark for the first time ever on Wednesday, notching up their third closing record in a row as emerging market funds continued to flow in from Asia and Brazil.
"We are still seeing foreign investors switching to Mexico, and volume has made the bull run solid," said Jose Gomez, an analyst at the Value brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC share index ended up 29.87 points, or 0.58 percent, at a record 5,212.89.
"Investors are continuing to bail out of Asia and Brazil," Gomez added.

Strong investment flows boosted trading volume to a heavy total of 166.7 million shares traded, dealers said. On the broad market, gainers outweighed sliders by 65 to 42 out of 129 stocks that changed hands.

The IPC reached as high as 5,235.45 points in earlier trade, but receded due to profit-taking on early pacemakers Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), financial group Bancomer and construction firm ICA, dealers said.

Telecommunications firm Telmex ended flat at 21.65 pesos ($2.70), Bancomer B shares shed 30 centavos (4 cents) to 5.44 pesos (70 cents) and ICA also declined by 30 centavos (4 cents) to end at 42.75 pesos ($5.49).
Analysts said Tuesday night's gains in primary rates were seen as a temporary spike whose effect on trade was confined to early profit-taking.
Financial firms in general stayed down, analysts added, as higher interest rates tend to increase their past-due loans problems.
Gomez said a rebound on Wall Street fuelled demand for American Depositary Receipts of Mexican companies and also helped the bourse to recover.

Holding company Accelsa, a market straggler, was the most active gainer, up 9 centavos (1 cent) to 1.97 pesos (25 cents) after an international brokerage upgraded the firm's Elamex subsidiary, dealers said.
